RE-MEASURED 2026-08-31, because Anthony returned to the restructure-before-optimise question and the numbers under it are ten days old. THREE OF THE FOUR PREMISES HAVE MOVED. THE ONE THAT DECIDES THE QUESTION HAS NOT.

═══ WHAT MOVED SINCE 2026-08-21 ═══
· (ii) A TARGET — was "1 Constraint in the entire design, and it is a SEMANTIC limit, not a budget. 0 DimensionAssessments. There is no stated performance target anywhere." NOW: 4 Constraints, 3 of them derived budgets, and ALL THREE MEASURED MET AND GUARDED TODAY (graph construction 1 ms, granularity N+2 reads, sweep 4 network builds).
· (iii) A MEASUREMENT — was "no benches directory, no criterion dependency, and not one Instant::now() or elapsed() in any test or tool. Nothing in this repository measures how long anything takes." NOW: the optimize skill has been run twice end to end, and a third measurement was taken today.
· (i) A WALL — was "0 of 10 subsystems publish a contract" and, separately, `fact:a-contract-is-the-one-thing-reflow2-cannot-attach-evidence-to` said no Interface could carry a check at all. BOTH MOVED. Interface was added to the VERIFIES `to` list on 2026-08-22 on Anthony's call, and measured today ALL THREE published contracts now carry a check: ifc:mcp-tools <- ver:the-served-tool-surface-matches-its-goldens, ifc:mcp-tools-http <- ver:shared-sessions, ifc:graph-export <- ver:the-export-survives-being-read-back. 22 Interfaces now: 9 required, 10 internal (was 4), 3 published.

⭐⭐ SO OPTION (e) WAS TAKEN AND IT WORKED. The 2026-08-21 node's cheapest option — "give one module a target and a measurement, and optimise it" — is exactly what happened, twice, and the budgets held. The two legs it called the urgent ones are supplied.

═══ 🛑 AND THE FINDING THAT DECIDES THE QUESTION IS UNCHANGED, RE-MEASURED TODAY ═══
    88 core .rs modules
    45 of them add methods to the SHARED `DesignGraph` struct, across 62 impl blocks
    67 of them DO define types of their own
    graph.rs alone carries 54 public methods on that one struct; temporal.rs 16, verify.rs 14, report.rs 12, detect.rs 12
(2026-08-21 read 54 modules / 43 sharing / 58 impl blocks. The ratio is the same and the absolute count has grown.)

TODAY'S SEAM SWEEP SAYS THE SAME THING FROM THE OTHER SIDE: of the 64 coupled pairs with no declared contract, 56 have `impl DesignGraph` on BOTH ends and ZERO cross a crate boundary (`fact:coupling-and-contract-are-recorded-in-vocabularies-that-never-meet`). Two independent measurements, one conclusion.

⭐ THE CONSEQUENCE, AND IT IS THE ANSWER TO "RESTRUCTURE FIRST, THEN OPTIMISE INSIDE THE BLACK BOX": modules own their OUTPUT TYPES and not their STATE. Every one reads the same store through the same accessors. So what a module can freely rework is its ALGORITHMS; what it cannot is its DATA REPRESENTATION — changing how anything is stored or indexed touches everybody. A CONTRACT AT THE SEAM DOES NOT CHANGE THAT, because the coupling runs through shared state rather than through the interface. Writing an ICD per subsystem would document boundaries that the code does not have.

⚠️ WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH. It does not say the god-struct SHOULD be broken up — that is a large change with its own risks, and `impl` blocks spread across modules is a normal and often deliberate Rust idiom for one aggregate. It says only that subsystem contracts are not the lever that produces substitutable or independently-optimisable modules while this holds. Whether anyone NEEDS that substitutability is a separate question the design has never answered; `dec:idea-swap-dynograph-foundation-as-the-substitutability-demo` is still open and is the only proposed test of it.

⚠️ AND IT DOES NOT MEASURE WHETHER THE SHARED STATE ACTUALLY COSTS ANYTHING TODAY. No optimisation has yet been blocked by it. The claim is structural, not an observed impediment — the two budgets that were met were both algorithmic, which is precisely the class this structure still permits.
